messages:
sara: FYI support ticket from Acme. Customer reports Private control plane mTLS failing after they flipped a new NAT appliance. Getting repeated TLS timeouts and no handshake completion. They attached tcpdump + openssl.

sara: Original customer excerpt:
> we started seeing control-plane API errors after the fw bump. app logs show "TLS handshake timeout" and our side retransmits ClientHello a few times then nothing. this started after we deployed vendor-xyz nat/gw.

sara: Paste of their `curl --verbose` to our control plane IP: 
```
*   Trying 10.20.30.40:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to controlplane.myredwood (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.20.30.40:443
* Connection #0 to host 10.20.30.40 left intact
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.20.30.40:443
```

sara: Their `openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.40:443 -msg -tlsextdebug` shows ClientHello sent, then no ServerHello: 
```
>>> TLS 1.3 Handshake, length=512
>>> ClientHello, msglen=512
(read) 
140 bytes from 10.20.30.40: No response
```

devin: Do they have packet captures? Any evidence of fragmentation or ICMP PMTU?

sara: They uploaded a small pcap. Key lines from tcpdump (filtered):
```
10:02:12.123456 IP 192.0.2.10.54321 > 10.20.30.40.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
10:02:12.123789 IP 10.20.30.40.443 > 192.0.2.10.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1360], length 0
10:02:12.124000 IP 192.0.2.10.54321 > 10.20.30.40.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1413, ack 1, len 1412
10:02:12.124200 IP 192.0.2.10 > 10.20.30.40: ICMP frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)
```
sara: ICMP "fragmentation needed" appears. Customer says their NAT device drops ICMP sometimes.

ram: OK that lines up with PMTU/MSS causing ClientHello + TLS extensions (SNI) to get fragmented and dropped. If ClientHello crosses path MTU and fragments, middleboxes sometimes drop fragments or strip options. That breaks SNI/ALPN and we never get ServerHello.

devin: Good call. Is the ClientHello being fragmented? The tcpdump shows a large push of 1412 bytes. For TLS1.3 EH clienthello with ALPN+SNI and large cipher lists, it can exceed MSS on a MTU-clamped path.

sara: They said setting `tcp_mtu_probing=1` on linux didn't change behavior. They also reported vendor NAT has a "smart fragment" mode off.

ram: Workarounds to suggest to customer:
- Force smaller MSS on egress (iptables or tunable) e.g. `ip route change ... mtu 1400` or `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360`
- Enable MSS clamp on the NAT appliance (vendor setting)
- Allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (fragmentation needed) through their egress firewall so PMTU discovery works
- If they cannot change network, suggest downgrading TLS record size? (not practical)

devin: Also ask them to capture server side tcpdump on our edge (we already have edge logs): our frontdoor shows receiving SYN/ACK and then we see a partial TLS record but no valid CH with SNI. Our logs show: `tls: incomplete client_hello from 192.0.2.10: missing server_name` at 10:02:12.12

sara: Customer tried `openssl s_client -servername controlplane.redwood.local -connect 10.20.30.40:443` and saw same silence. They cannot change NAT policy without a change window; asking for a temporary mitigation from our side.

ram: From our side options:
- Accept non-SNI handshakes on that dedicated IP? risky and not recommended.
- Temporarily allow a compat-algo: accept smaller ClientHello fragments? No, we can't fix their middlebox.
- We can add a small HTTP health endpoint that doesn't rely on TLS SNI for token refresh? But control plane auth requires mTLS and client cert validation so that won't bypass.

devin: Best is to push network guidance. Also ask them to test `curl --max-time 10 --ciphers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 -v` to see if reducing extension list helps (unlikely).

sara: I've sent guidance: enable ICMP fragment unreach, configure MSS clamp to 1360, or schedule NAT appliance change. Customer asked if we can change anything on Redwood Private to help during their maintenance window.

ram: Offer: we can schedule a 1-hour troubleshooting window where we capture simultaneous pcaps and try to reproduce while they toggle NAT settings. But note we cannot change TLS policy.

sara: Customer accepted the 1h session for tomorrow 14:00 UTC. I've opened internal ticket INC-54321 and pinned the pcap + openssl logs. @devin @ram please join.

supportbot: Ticket INC-54321 created and linked to GRA-9988. Reminder: include pcap in evidence in the ticket, and redact any private cert material.

devin: I'll bring a packet analysis checklist. Ram, please prepare notes on MSS/iptable commands and vendor config examples (vendor-xyz NAT).

ram: Will do. Also recommend customer check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and `ip route` for lower MTU hops.

sara: Thanks all. I'll coordinate invite and add customer contact details to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
